paragraphs.text: Haste is a keyword ability that allows a creature to circumvent summoning sickness . Creatures with haste can attack or use activated abilities with the or symbol in the activation cost even if they have not been continuously controlled by a player since the beginning of that player's most recent turn.

Summoning sickness is one of the greater liabilities of creatures, as if the creature is removed on the opponent's following turn it generally means it contributed nothing to the game. While enters triggers is one way to mitigate this, they tend toward being attrition-based. In contrast, haste is a tempo-based solution. It also plays better in Constructed as it is more effective against creatureless or creature-light decks, than in Limited, where the midrange-heavy environment often means the player casting the haste creature is largely tapped out, hence attacking into a stalled board or combat tricks.

Haste has been in Magic since the original Limited Edition Alpha ' 's Nether Shadow , though it did not have a keyword at the time and was simply spelled out in the rules text. In R&D , it was known by the nickname Celerity . Players used to refer to it as Raging . It wasn't until the Sixth Edition rules change that it got added as a keyword ability.

Haste has been rotated around the color wheel , initially being in black and green ; it has now been placed primary in red , before black and green. Lately, green has moved up to secondary place along with black. Green getting haste was a nod to constructed as a way to recover after board wipes. Many mechanics grant haste inherently, such as Dash , Blitz , Riot and temporary control , all of which are focused in red and green. Some mechanics that are not usually in red or green can grant haste as a gameplay concession, as Suspend , Unearth variants, and land animation like Awaken and Earthbending require haste to achieve the intended result.

For Future Sight , R&D explored the idea of putting haste on blue creatures with Defender and 0 power, where the haste was about using the activated ability right away rather than attacking ( Bonded Fetch ). After 16 years of floating this idea, the second blue haster was printed in Streets of New Capenna with Errant, Street Artist .
Haste counters were introduced with Indominus Rex, Alpha in Jurassic World Collection .

The Gingerbrute ability is a slang term used by Magic R&D for “can only be blocked by creatures with haste", giving the impression of "so fast they have to be caught be similarly fast things". Both creatures that have the ability have haste; both noncreatures that grant it also grant the target haste. Speed, Young Avenger is both in that he both has haste and can grant it to those with haste. It is a type of evasion .

While haste has been associated with creatures being exceptionally fast (in addition to merely quick reactions) since at least Odyssey ( Need for Speed ), Universes Beyond sets such as Sonic Superdrop and Marvel Super Heroes have made haste a standard inclusion on cards representing characters with super speed (e.g., Super Speed , Sonic the Hedgehog , Speed, Young Avenger ). Cards representing groups can get haste if at least one member possesses super speed (e.g., Power Pack , The Squadron Sinister ).
